#+TITLE: Org slides

Copy =starter.org=, open it in Emacs, and use =C-c C-e l P= to export
Beamer PDF, or =C-c C-e l O= to export and open it. Restart Emacs once
to pick up the installed PVS/SAL mode autoloads. Use capital =P= or =O=;
lowercase =p= or =o= selects ordinary LaTeX export and loses Beamer layouts.

The file uses ordinary Org and Beamer, with Computer Modern serif text
and Inconsolata code. Code has no background fill or border. These settings
are ordinary LaTeX header lines at the top of the Org file.
Edit the title, author, date, and institute lines at the top. The institute
contains the affiliation and presentation location. Uncomment the
=titlegraphic= line to add a logo or other title image.

Each top-level heading is a slide. Copy the two-column example to place
text and images side by side; edit =BEAMER_COL= for widths. Replace either
column's content with text, an image link, or code. An image link outside
the columns fills a normal slide; =ATTR_LATEX= controls its size.

Use =#+begin_src pvs= or =#+begin_src sal= for highlighted code.
Org's built-in =engraved= backend uses the actual PVS and SAL Emacs modes
through the standard GNU ELPA package =engrave-faces= (already installed).
Keep the Local Variables block at the end of each deck to enable it.
Other source languages work through their Emacs modes too.

There are no build scripts, custom exporters, themes, or language lexers.
The sample image is =assets/decay.pdf=; copy it with the starter or replace
its link with your own image. PDF, PNG, and JPEG work with normal export.

Nested headings have different typography as well as size. See the
"Nested headings" slide in =starter.org=:

- =*= is the slide title.
- =**= is large, bold, and uses the Beamer heading color.
- =***= is normal size, bold, and black.
- =****= and deeper are small, italic, and black.

The =slideblockdepth= LaTeX header lines control the sizes, weight, shape,
and color. The hierarchy follows nested titled blocks; column labels stay
hidden. Keep =H:1= so top-level headings remain individual slides.
